source_spans.locator: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 360, published pp.815-816, Abstract/Introduction: sensory causes are inferred with learned hierarchical models; context-sensitive prior expectations and recurrent mismatch reduction are proposed

Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 360, published pp.820-821, equations (3.4)-(3.7): inference and learning optimize the same free-energy objective; under the stated Gaussian model, free-energy minimization is expressed as weighted discrepancy reduction

Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 360, published p.822, equations (3.8)-(3.10), Cortical hierarchies and empirical Bayes: higher-level densities act as priors on subordinate causes; high-level causes determine context-sensitive prior expectations; covariance/precision parameters weight uncertainty

Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 360, published pp.822-823, equation (3.11) and cortical-connectivity implications: current cause estimates are driven by mismatch at the current and immediately lower levels; descending predictions and ascending mismatch signals use reciprocal but functionally asymmetric connections

Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 360, published p.824, Figure 2 and Functional organization: representational estimates minimize both discrepancy from their predicted value and mismatch incurred by their prediction of the level below; these correspond to prior and likelihood constraints

Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 360, published pp.825-826, dynamic-model boundary and cortical-physiology section: specific dynamic algorithms are not fixed here; backward influences provide contextual predictions, incompatible lower-level input generates mismatch that drives higher-level change until reconciliation

Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 360, published p.826, cortical-physiology decomposition: one functional subpopulation encodes conditional cause estimates while another encodes mismatch; as inference converges, lower-level mismatch is suppressed and higher-level representations emerge

conditions: sensory causes are inferred with a multi-level generative scheme in which a state at one level predicts the state at the level below
the source's explicit static derivation assumes Gaussian stochastic terms and, for the simple neuronal implementation, conditional independence and deterministic recognition
covariance or precision parameters determine the weighting of discrepancies at each level
population: sensory cortical systems interpreted through the source's theoretical model and reviewed neurophysiological evidence
substrate: neighboring levels of a cortical hierarchy with reciprocal ascending, descending, and within-level interactions
task: infer the most likely hidden causes of sensory input while using context from higher levels and evidence from lower levels
temporal_scope: during perceptual inference, recurrent local updates continue until weighted discrepancies across neighboring levels are reduced
the source distinguishes this fast inference process from slower parameter learning; the bounded claim here concerns the inference architecture rather than the learning rule

nodes.description: activity or sensory information at the immediately subordinate level that the current level attempts to explain
conditional estimate of a supraordinate hidden cause that supplies contextual information to the level below
conditional estimate of the hidden cause represented at the current level
predicted value of the current-level cause generated from the estimate at the level above
weighted difference between the current-level cause estimate and the value predicted from the level above
prediction of subordinate-level activity generated from the current-level cause estimate
weighted difference between subordinate-level input and the prediction generated by the current-level estimate
inverse-variance weighting associated with uncertainty in discrepancies and prior expectations
state in which the weighted discrepancies associated with both the prior constraint and the fit to the subordinate level are jointly reduced
forward influence by which mismatch from the level below changes cause estimates at the current or supraordinate level
backward influence by which a higher cause estimate generates predictions of activity at the lower level

relations.description: a supraordinate cause estimate generates the context-sensitive predicted value that functions as a prior constraint on the current level
the predicted value from the level above constrains the conditional estimate represented at the current level
deviation of the current-level estimate from the higher-level prediction forms the locally weighted prior-side discrepancy
the current-level cause estimate generates a prediction of activity or input at the immediately subordinate level
incompatibility between subordinate input and the prediction from the current level forms the likelihood-side discrepancy
mismatch from the level below drives changes in the current-level cause estimate through the ascending influence
the current-level prior-side discrepancy also contributes locally to changes in the current-level estimate
the contribution of the current-level discrepancy depends on its covariance or inverse-variance weighting
the contribution of subordinate mismatch is likewise precision weighted in the source's Gaussian formulation
the inferred current-level state is selected by jointly reducing the prior-side discrepancy and the mismatch generated by its prediction of the level below
subordinate mismatch is carried forward as a driving influence on supraordinate representational estimates
higher-level estimates are conveyed backward as predictions of lower-level activity
the two reciprocal directions are functionally asymmetric: ascending influences carry mismatch that drives estimates, whereas descending influences generate contextual predictions
